cases.rationale: scope not accepted while everything else would establish
presence neither true nor false; closed-world premises otherwise hold (would be VIOLATED if presence were read as absent)
route observation not accepted while everything else would establish
an effect is reported but its observation is not accepted; must not become VIOLATED
accepted effect source but effect_seen false (second half of the compound guard)
observed_state present, expected_state absent (first half of the compound guard)
effect-observation guard precedes scope guard
presence guard precedes mandatory-admission guard
mandatory-admission guard precedes window guard
window guard precedes coverage guard
route guard precedes operation-binding guard
operation-binding guard precedes outside-PEP guard
outside-PEP guard precedes effect-observation guard
effect-unknown guard precedes effect-window guard
effect-window guard precedes control guard
read-back availability precedes source acceptance
source acceptance precedes target/predicate binding
target/predicate binding precedes freshness
freshness precedes settlement
settlement precedes state-value presence
valid control missing is the only failing premise, so erasing it must not make the claim decisive
integer 1 is not the boolean true; strict checker stays inconclusive (truthiness would give VIOLATED)
string "true" is not the boolean true (truthiness would give ESTABLISHED)
non-empty object is not the boolean true (truthiness would give ESTABLISHED)
strings that differ only in case are different states (case folding would give ESTABLISHED)
the same members in another order are a different list (sorting lists would give ESTABLISHED)
equal keys with different values are different mappings (comparing keys only would give ESTABLISHED)
a JSON object is an unordered set of members (RFC 8259 section 4): the same members in another key order are the same state (comparing insertion order would give VIOLATED)
key order is not member order: a list inside a mapping keeps its order, so E19 lifted one level is still a different state (sorting nested lists would give ESTABLISHED)
key-order independence holds at every depth, not only at the top level (sorting only top-level keys would give VIOLATED)

rejections.rationale: an unknown claim name has no assessor and must be refused, not assessed as any other claim
a null claim is not a claim
observations must be a mapping; a list of premises is malformed input
null observations are malformed input, not an empty observation set
a float is outside the fixture value vocabulary; the checker must refuse rather than compare it
validation recurses into lists: an invalid value at depth is still invalid
validation recurses into mappings: an invalid value at depth is still invalid
a premise in the scope is validated like a premise in the observations
only synthetic_fixture premises are accepted; the production guard must refuse every other premise source
an empty premise source is not the synthetic source
